data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Iphlgenia is the goddess of purification and prophecy. She is the daughter of King Tmosios and Chloris, and is famously known for her sacrifice to Artemis. Her name is derived from the Greek words 'iphlos' (pure) and 'genos' (race, kind). The name Iphlgenia carries the meaning “Goddess of purification” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Iphlgenia usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of purification and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Iphlgenia, in Greek mythology, was a revered goddess associated with purification and prophecy. Her story, which involves a prophecy regarding her life and a costly test of her devotion to the gods, has been retold through various mediums, including poetry, drama, and art, throughout history. This has led to her name being passed down through generations, and her cultural influence extending beyond the Greek world.
data.spiritual_significance: For ancient Greeks, Iphlgenia represented the idea of purification and the power of prophecy. The goddess was believed to cleanse individuals and spaces of impurities and to provide insight into the future through divine revelations. Her story serves as a reminder of the importance of maintaining spiritual purity and seeking guidance from the divine.
